debate_title: Should frontier AI developers be legally liable for harms...

conflicts.point: Whether foundational AI model weights are analogous to manufactured physical products like aircraft or traditional software libraries regarding upstream liability.

positions.stance: Base models are general-purpose mathematical artifacts that evolve infinitely through downstream fine-tuning, making them identical to traditional software libraries rather than physical airframes.
Complex AI systems carry systemic scaling risks that require aviation-style pre-deployment safety baselines and certification.

conflicts.point: Whether downstream deployers possess sufficient technical context and financial capital to bear independent tort liability for model failures.

positions.stance: Local deployers interface directly with end users, maintain local audit logs, and command the capital reserves necessary to settle tort claims independently.
Upstream vendors deliberately withhold internal telemetry and diagnostic tools, creating an information asymmetry that leaves downstream deployers vulnerable without access to error logs.

verdicts.conflict: Whether foundational AI model weights are analogous to manufactured physical products like aircraft or traditional software libraries regarding upstream liability.
verdicts.rationale: Both analogies capture partial truths about complex software artifacts. Physical product liability accounts for systemic scaling risks, but software library analogies better reflect the infinite mutability of open weights through downstream fine-tuning. Neither camp has established a definitive legal framework that reconciles these contradictory technological properties.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Courts establishing a novel legal precedent that either classifies general-purpose code as a manufactured product or exempts it entirely.

verdicts.conflict: Whether downstream deployers possess sufficient technical context and financial capital to bear independent tort liability for model failures.
verdicts.rationale: Skeptics provide stronger evidence regarding information asymmetry, demonstrating that upstream vendors routinely restrict access to internal error logs and training telemetry. This leaves downstream operators legally exposed for harms they lack the technical capability to diagnose or prevent. Accelerationists offer theoretical market arguments but fail to disprove the existence of this telemetry gap.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Upstream developers providing standardized diagnostic tools and transparent telemetry to all downstream deployers without restrictive licensing terms.
